title: Supplemental ja-to-zh-Hant singing and humming QA bank

provenance.sentence_provenance: Original Japanese sentences written for this draft. No exam, textbook, game, or other external sentence text was copied.
provenance.reference_provenance: Provisional Taiwan Traditional Chinese references drafted by the first-party data author. They are not model gold.

purpose: Provide one matched public development contrast for the general singing sense of 歌う and the humming sense of 口ずさむ.
level_note: Approximate sentence difficulty only. These are not JLPT questions or JLPT certification. The contrast verb 口ずさむ may be above the simple sentence level.

items.jp: 放課後、私は歌を歌いました。
semantic_checks: The predicate uses the general singing sense of 歌う, not specifically humming.
The sentence is a polite past statement.
semantic_unknowns: The source does not provide lyrics or mention accompaniment.
This context does not define every use of 歌う.

stable: The pair keeps the speaker, after-class setting, song object, and polite past statement constant.
changed: This row uses 歌う in its general singing sense.
limits: The pair does not specify lyrics, accompaniment, or performance style.

items.jp: 放課後、私は歌を口ずさみました。
semantic_checks: The predicate uses 口ずさむ; retain the humming sense instead of collapsing it to generic singing.
The sentence is a polite past statement.
semantic_unknowns: The source does not provide lyrics or mention accompaniment.
The source does not specify volume, lip position, or whether lyrics were vocalized.
This context does not define every use of 口ずさむ.

stable: The pair keeps the speaker, after-class setting, song object, and polite past statement constant.
changed: This row uses 口ずさむ in a humming context.
limits: The pair does not specify lyrics, accompaniment, or performance style.

review_and_adoption.process: Independent language review and adoption must be recorded in a separate data-only PR before any rule uses these rows for acceptance.
review_and_adoption.scope_limit: This matched pair checks one shared context. It does not cover every sense or context of either verb.
